t:
For necessary expenses of the Food and Drug Administration, including hire and purchase of passenger motor vehicles; for rental of special purpose space in the District of Columbia or elsewhere; and for miscellaneous and emergency expenses of enforcement activities, authorized and approved by the Secretary and to be accounted for solely on the Secretary’s certificate, not to exceed $25,000; $904,694,000, of which not to exceed $84,723,000 in fees pursuant to section 736 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act may be credited to this appropriation and remain available until expended: Provided, That fees derived from applications  received during fiscal year 1996 shall be subject to the fiscal year 1996 limitation: Provided further, That none of these funds shall be used to develop, establish, or operate any program of user fees authorized by 31 U.S.C. 9701.
In addition, fees pursuant to section 354 of the Public Health Service Act may be credited to this account, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding FDA expenses and governing how user fees are credited to the account. The tempting reading is that the references to "applications" and industry-paid fees bring outside parties in, but applying for something and paying fees is not participating in a federal decision. Nothing in the section calls for a comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: For necessary expenses of the Food and Drug Administration, including hire and purchase of passenger motor vehicles

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that sets funding amounts for the Food and Drug Administration and says how user fees are credited and limited. Its one mention of outside parties is the fee-paying 'applications', and the definition excludes applications. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders or right to sue, so the keyword does not show participation.
opus.s: Provided, That fees derived from applications  received during fiscal year 1996 shall be subject to the fiscal year 1996 limitation
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the text mentions "applications" and fees under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. That fails because these are applications that companies submit to the FDA, and the section only covers how the fees from them are credited to the appropriation. The definition excludes applications. No outside party is consulted before any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for the Food and Drug Administration and specifies how user fees from applications can be credited to the account. It does not require or recommend any form of public participation, consultation, or advisory input from outside parties. The mention of 'applications' refers to the source of fees, not a participatory process, and the definition explicitly excludes applications from the scope of participation.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses of the Food and Drug Administration... $904,694,000, of which not to exceed $84,723,000 in fees pursuant to section 736 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act may be credited to this appropriation
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "applications" implies a process where applicants participate in a decision. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" (and by extension, licenses or permits) are not participation. Furthermore, the text is primarily an appropriations clause detailing funding limits and fee structures, not a procedural mandate for public consultation or advisory input.
